# cloud-hands.bin — build notes

> v2 (skinned 22-joint sequence, `taiji-sequence.bin` = v2b: slow, fluid, generated arms + choreographed lower body; records v2a and arms-only) is described in the **v2** section at the end of this file.

Hero motion pack in the `hmmh-motion-1` layout (`shared/MOTION_FORMAT.md`). SMPL-X body doing Tai Chi "Cloud Hands" (云手).
**The motion is procedurally generated by the source project, not recorded from a person.**

**Shipped file: `cloud-hands.bin` is the seamless CYCLE version.** It holds one exact 2.56 s motion period in 48 frames at fps 18.75, with `loop: "cycle"`.
The every-second-frame pingpong version is kept for the record as `cloud-hands-pingpong.bin`; its numbers are in the last sections.

Both files were built by `tools/motion_pack.py`:
- cycle: `build --frames period`
- pingpong: `build --frames every2`

Previews in this folder: `preview-00.png`, `preview-12.png`, `preview-24.png`, `preview-36.png`, `preview-47.png`. They show frames 0/12/24/36/47 of the installed cycle file at 800×800 (three.js 0.186.1 test page, headless Chromium). Frames 47 and 0 look the same, which shows the seam is continuous.

## Source (read-only)
Repo `smplx_meridian_project` (local checkout `~/Documents/GitHub/smplx_meridian_project`), folder `website/public/data/mesh/`:
- `manifest.json` → `actions.G07` (云手 "Move hands like clouds", 96 frames, 30 fps, 3.2 s). Decode `m = offset_m + u16 * scale_m_per_uint` per axis.
- `g07.vertices.u16.bin` — [96, 10475, 3] uint16, frame-major, pelvis-centred body-local.
- `faces.u16.bin` — 20908×3 uint16, SMPL-X native winding (byte-identical to `SMPLX_NEUTRAL.npz` `f`).
- `models/smplx/SMPLX_NEUTRAL.npz` — read for `J_regressor` (axis checks) and skin `weights` (pelvis/foot/part labels) only.

## Orientation: identity rotation
The manifest frame is already right-handed, +Y superior, +Z anterior, +X subject-left. Seen from the front (camera on +Z), +X runs from the viewer's left to right. So the rotation is **R = I**, applied to every frame. Checked with SMPL-X joints at frame 0: left hip − right hip x = +0.122 m; head − pelvis y = +0.617 m; nose tip (v9120) − head joint z = +0.117 m; left foot − left ankle z = +0.119 m; pelvis joint = (−0.1, −0.7, −0.3) mm. The feet stay planted: sole vertices move ≤ 7 mm across the clip and foot yaw changes ≤ 0.3°.

## Mesh (same for both files)
1. Dropped the two closed eyeball shells (vertices 9383–10474: 1,092 vertices, 2,176 faces). They sit inside the head and would cost triangles.
2. Capped the only hole in the body surface, the 32-edge mouth loop, with a 30-face zig-zag strip built from existing vertices. The reference surface is then watertight, winding-consistent and genus 0, with signed volume +0.0754 m³, i.e. CCW-outward.
3. Ran open3d quadric decimation once, on source frame 0 of this surface, targeting 3,600 triangles. Result: **V = 1,802, T = 3,600**, 5,400 edges, watertight, winding-consistent, Euler 2.
4. Mapped each decimated vertex to its closest point on the full frame-0 surface (open3d RaycastingScene → triangle id + barycentrics). The snap moves vertices by max 2.75 mm, p99 1.04 mm, mean 0.08 mm. Every frame is then rebuilt as `p = Σ bᵢ · V_frame[hostᵢ]`, so the low-poly body sits exactly on the full surface at every frame.
5. Checks on the 48 dequantised frames of the shipped file: CCW-outward at every frame (min signed volume 0.0743 m³, no flip needed); 0 unreferenced vertices; 0 repeated-index faces; min face area 22 mm²; min angle 2.3°.

## Frames, fps, loop (shipped cycle file)
- **The motion is exactly periodic.** The period is 76.8 source frames = 2.56 s, found by a sub-frame search, and frame t and t + 76.8 differ by 0.03 mm on average. The 96-frame source clip holds 1.25 cycles.
- **Resampling.** The 48 pack frames sit at source times k · 1.6 frames (k = 0…47), i.e. fps 30 × 48 / 76.8 = **18.75**, one period long. Each pack frame is a linear blend of the two neighbouring 30 fps source frames; pack frames 0, 5, 10, … fall exactly on source frames 0, 8, 16, …. The blend spacing is 33 ms. At twice that spacing (67 ms) the measured blend error is 1.9 mm max, so these blends should be well under 1 mm (an estimate, not measured).
- **loop = "cycle"**, because the seam is invisible: the jump from frame 47 to frame 0 averages **7.4 mm** (max 61 mm at the hand). A normal frame-to-frame step is 6.8 mm (median; range 4.2–9.0 mm; 7.2 / 7.5 mm at the two ends). The seam is one ordinary step, with no reversal.
- `keyframes` [0, 12, 24, 36].

## Reconstruction error (shipped cycle file, all 48 frames, dequantised, mm)
| measure | max | p99 (worst frame) | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| decimated vertex → closest point on full surface | **0.018** | 0.014 | 0.005 |
| decimated faces (10 samples/face) → full surface | 8.66 | 2.78 | 0.60 |
| full-res vertices → decimated surface | 8.89 | 4.73 | 1.08 |
| uint16 quantisation | 0.019 | — | — |

- The vertex error meets the contract's ≤ 5 mm (only quantisation error remains).
- **The two-sided surface error (8.9 mm max) is accepted** by the coordinator's decision. It exceeds 5 mm on 0.7 % of full-res vertices at the worst frame: ears 35 vertices, fingertips 17, the armpit/upper-back skin fold 11, a toe 2. These are thin features that 3.6 k triangles cannot resolve.
- Budget sweep (max / p99 of full → decimated): T 3000 → 10.3 / 5.7 mm (452 KB); **T 3600 → 8.9 / 4.7 mm (542 KB)**; T 3900 → 8.9 / 4.2 mm (587 KB). A larger T does not remove the ear/armpit maximum.
- Decimating on the SMPL-X rest template instead of frame 0 was worse: 14.2 / 5.8 mm, because of the fingers.

## Header-derived values (shipped cycle file)
- `groundY` = −0.959667 m: the lowest decimated vertex over all frames, which is a foot vertex. The full-res minimum is −0.960142, so the decimated sole sits 0.5 mm higher.
- `centre` = [−0.002896, −0.026051]: mean (x, z) of the full-res SMPL-X pelvis-region vertices at frame 0 (434 vertices whose largest skin weight is on the pelvis). Using the 157 decimated pelvis-region vertices instead gives [−0.0036, −0.0475]; that estimate depends on where the decimation happened to put vertices. The pelvis joint itself is at 0. The feet centroid is at x −0.089, z −0.001, because the stance is narrow and asymmetric.
- `bounds` min [−0.756461, −0.959667, −0.437866], max [0.797378, 0.768457, 0.536715] over all frames.
- Extra header field `axes` (a string spelling out the axis convention). It is additive; no contract field was changed.

## File (shipped)
`cloud-hands.bin` = **541,524 bytes** = 4 (headerLen) + 944 (header, space-padded) + 21,600 (faces 3600×3 u16) + 518,976 (48×1802×3 u16).
- The installed file is byte-identical to a fresh deterministic rebuild (`build --frames period`), and that rebuild passed the internal round-trip assert: vertices within half a quantisation step, ≤ 13.2 µm per axis.
- The independent reader `read_pack` on the installed file returns the build header exactly, with 48 × 1802 × 3 values, faces in range, and `bounds`/`groundY` equal to the decoded data.

Header JSON, verbatim; the padding is 3 trailing spaces:

## Alternative kept for the record: `cloud-hands-pingpong.bin` (not shipped)
- **Frames:** source frames 0, 2, …, 94 at fps 15 (3.2 s), 48 frames, same mesh (V 1,802, T 3,600), 541,524 bytes, loop "pingpong".
- **Why not cycle for this version:** the jump from frame 47 to 0 averages 62.6 mm (max 455 mm at the right hand) against a median step of 8.4 mm (range 5.2–11.3), so a cycle seam would be visible.
- **Why it was not shipped:** pingpong reverses at frame 0 in the middle of the motion (step 9.0 mm), which reads as a short "rewind". At frame 47 the motion is slower (step 5.5 mm).
- **Errors:** vertex 0.018 mm max; faces → full 8.67 mm max / 2.79 p99; full → faces 8.90 mm max / 4.72 p99. The viewer's linear interpolation at the skipped 30 fps frames is off by 1.94 mm max / 1.74 p99.
- **Header-derived values:** `groundY` −0.959667; `centre` [−0.002896, −0.026051]; `bounds` min [−0.756461, −0.959667, −0.437586], max [0.797397, 0.768457, 0.536858].

Header JSON, verbatim; the padding is 2 trailing spaces:

## Known issues (not fixed)
- 29 coarse faces, on the ears, feet and fingertips, have normals more than 90° away from the full-res surface under them. 27 of them already come out of QEM before snapping. The winding is consistent; these faces just span thin features. They are not visible at hero scale in the previews.
- Some decimated edges stretch up to 3.7× and shrink to 0.2× over the clip. The full-res mesh itself stretches 0.08–4.2× in the same shoulder/armpit region (SMPL-X skinning), so this is inherited from the source and is not a mapping error.
- What the motion looks like, from the source: narrow stance, feet planted, shoulder line yaws ±21°. The right wrist sweeps front to back (z −0.36 … +0.40 m) while the left wrist stays out to the side (z 0.02–0.13 m). From the front it reads as an alternating side-to-side arm sweep, not a textbook symmetric Cloud Hands.
- The shipped fps is 18.75 (non-integer), so the viewer must take fps from the header.

## Licence
Body: SMPL-X (MPI-IS) under its research licence; decimated web mesh; motion procedurally generated, not recorded.

PY=~/Documents/GitHub/smplx_meridian_project/.venv/bin/python
$PY tools/motion_pack.py build --frames period --out shared/assets/motion --stats <scratch>/cycle_stats.json      # shipped cloud-hands.bin
$PY tools/motion_pack.py build --frames every2 --out <scratch> --stats <scratch>/pingpong_stats.json               # then rename to cloud-hands-pingpong.bin
~/tools/.venv/bin/python tools/motion_pack.py preview --bin shared/assets/motion/cloud-hands.bin --workdir <scratch> --png-dir shared/assets/motion --frames 0,12,24,36,47
```

# v2 — `taiji-sequence.bin` (skinned sequence, `hmmh-motion-2`)

## What ships
- **`taiji-sequence.bin` = v2b, "slow and fluid"** (194,276 bytes).
  - Same six generated forms in the same order, same layout.
  - Re-timed to **792 frames = 26.4 s at 30 fps**: 6 segments of 132 frames (4.4 s), each opening with a 30-frame (1.0 s) minimum-jerk cross-fade.
  - Choreographed lower body, phase-lagged upper body, every curve low-passed.
  - Previews: `preview-seq-00 … 11.png`, frames 0, 66, …, 726, three.js `SkinnedMesh`, camera yaw 30°.
  - Curves before/after smoothing: `curves-v2b.png`.
- **Kept for the record:**
  - `taiji-sequence-v2a.bin` (141,708 B; 504 frames, the first choreographed build). Previews `preview-seq-v2a-00 … 11.png`. The user found it stiff ("动作僵硬，不够流畅").
  - `taiji-sequence-arms-only.bin` (141,292 B; generated motion only). Previews `preview-seq-arms-only-00 … 07.png`.
- **All three rebuild byte-identically** with the current `tools/motion_pack.py` (commands at the end), and so does v1 `cloud-hands.bin`.

## Generated by the project vs added here (v2b)
| part of the motion | source |
|---|---|
| arm, spine, neck, head rotations of 天地合一 / 野马分鬃 / 搂膝拗步 / 倒卷肱 / 金鸡独立 / 云手 | **generated** (`body_pose_axis_angle_rad`), re-timed: each 96-frame clip is resampled by a cubic spline (sign-continuous quaternions) to 162 frames, i.e. played at 0.59× speed |
| arm + spine ×1.3 about each clip's mean | applied here |
| min-jerk (quintic) 30-frame cross-fades and the closed loop | applied here |
| wrists trail the forearms (5-frame lag, ≤ 12°), head follows the leading hand (yaw ±8°, pitch ±3°, 6-frame lag), chest breathing (±1.5° flexion, 4.4 s), spine counter-rotation, 3° torso turn at the kick top | applied here |
| pelvis: weight shift following the arms (waist leads by 9 frames), sway ±1.2 cm (0.265 Hz), sink 5 → 8 cm oscillating once per form, yaw ±28.5° | **choreographed** |
| legs: planted IK stance, right heel kick (2.2 s), left knee raise (2.0 s hold), raised right arm in the hold | **choreographed** |
| shoulder-abduction clearance bumps (left ≤ 6°, right ≤ 24°) where a hand would enter the body | applied here (automatic) |
| Gaussian low-pass σ = 5 frames (circular) of every curve | applied here |

**How the low-pass is applied.**
- The **upper-body joints** (spine, neck, head, collars, shoulders, elbows, wrists) are smoothed after assembly, in the tangent space at each joint's mean rotation. So transitions, wrist lag, head follow and the raised-arm overlay are all smoothed.
- The **choreographed layer** is smoothed through its drivers: pelvis x/z/sink/yaw, foot swing targets, kick/raise phase curves and blend weights.
- The **legs** are then re-solved by IK from the smoothed pelvis, so planted feet stay exact. Smoothing the leg angles directly would make the feet slide.
- **Root y** gets the floor solve, smoothed with σ = 2 (change ≤ 0.02 mm).

## Step 1 — contact sheets (why choreography was needed; unchanged)
The 16 generated actions (sheets in the build session's scratchpad, `…/scratchpad/motion/v2/contact/`) are upper-body arm swings on locked, straight legs. Leg-joint motion is 0° in 14 of 16, and the spine moves ≤ 10°.
- **Picked:** G04, G08, G12, G06, G09, G07.
- **Rejected:**
  - look-alikes: G10, G13;
  - small arm motion: G05, G03;
  - signal motions: SYN01, SYN02, OPT01;
  - static: G01, G02;
  - broken: heel_kick G11 (foot 4.3 cm through the floor).

## Step 2 — timeline (v2b)
| # | segment | frames (incl.) | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bring sky and earth together (天地合一) | 0–131 | 0.0–4.4 |
| 2 | Part the wild horse's mane (野马分鬃) | 132–263 | 4.4–8.8 |
| 3 | Brush knee and twist step (搂膝拗步) | 264–395 | 8.8–13.2 |
| 4 | Drive the monkey away (倒卷肱) | 396–527 | 13.2–17.6 |
| 5 | Golden rooster stands on one leg (金鸡独立) | 528–659 | 17.6–22.0 |
| 6 | Move hands like clouds (云手) | 660–791 | 22.0–26.4 |

- Each segment opens with the 30-frame min-jerk blend from the previous clip; the first one blends from 云手, which closes the loop.
- Periodic components divide the loop exactly, so the wrap is continuous:
  - sway: 7 cycles (113.1 frames ≈ 0.265 Hz);
  - breathing: 6 cycles (132 frames = 4.4 s);
  - sink: one cycle per segment, 5.0 cm at segment boundaries and 8.0 cm mid-form.
- **Heel kick** (inside 倒卷肱):
  - Foot off the floor 426 → 492 (66 frames = **2.2 s**).
  - Quintic rise to the top at 454.
  - **0.5 s at the top that still moves (454–469):** hip 68 → 72°, knee 12 → 9° (the foot keeps rising), torso turns +3°.
  - Quintic fall; lands at 492.
  - Standing knee ≈ 20°.
- **Knee raise** (金鸡独立):
  - Foot off the floor 538 → 650.
  - **2.0 s hold 564–624, still moving:**
    - pelvis sways −21.1 → −18.7 cm;
    - pelvis yaw drifts −0.7…+2.9°;
    - standing knee breathes 13.2…16.8° (±1.8°);
    - raised thigh and knee drift 77–82° / 92–97°;
    - raised right arm drifts ≤ 4.4°.

## Step 3 — rest mesh and skin (unchanged)
- **Rest pose:** SMPL-X neutral zero pose, hands at the mean, pelvis at the origin, canonical +Y up / +Z front / +X subject-left.
- **Mesh:** QEM decimation to **V 1,802 / T 3,600**, barycentric map.
- **Weights:** folded to 22 joints, top 4, uint8 summing to 255.

## Step 4 — choreography (v2a base, v2b changes)
- **Stance:**
  - Both feet planted flat at fixed spots: left (+0.239, −0.875, +0.053) m, right (−0.262, −0.877, +0.062) m, toes out 15°.
  - Each leg is solved every frame by an exact two-bone IK with the knee over the toes. No planted leg reaches full extension (asserted).
- **Weight shift follows the arms:**
  - The signal is the mean wrist x, smoothed and taken 9 frames ahead (the waist leads).
  - It is mapped with tanh(m / 0.12) / tanh(0.17 / 0.12). This is gentler than v2a's saturating map, so the pelvis no longer dwells at the extremes.
  - Pelvis x ±9 cm (+ sway); yaw ±28.5°, with the chest turning ≈ 60 % of it.
- **One-leg phases:**
  - The pelvis moves through a pre-lift bow (both feet still planted) to the support pose (hip over the support ankle).
  - The lifting foot rises 7 cm and draws in under its hip by IK before the keyed kick or raise takes over in the air. Landing reverses it.
  - In v2b every edge of this is a quintic, and the kick/raise angles follow a phase variable along a pose path (lift → chamber → top), so no joint stops at intermediate keys.
- **Bow extremes** (55 frames with |follow| > 0.9): front knee 33.3–43.7°, rear 10.0–31.2°, sink 5.5–7.9 cm, shift 6.9–10.3 cm, yaw 22.8–30.2°. The knees bend deeper than in v2a because the sink now reaches 8 cm mid-form, as asked.

| p99 joint speed | 3.58 | 2.34 |
| root translation max jerk | 2.73 mm/frame³ | 0.26 mm/frame³ |

- Per-joint max speed after smoothing:
  - kicking knee 8.5;

  - left knee 3.4;
  - shoulder L 2.7;
  - pelvis 2.4;
  - elbows / wrists ≤ 1.8;

- The fastest point is the kicking foot at 104 mm/frame (3.1 m/s).

**Contact and clearance:**
- No foot below the floor in any frame (asserted).
- Planted feet sit 0–1.3 mm above the floor and slide ≤ 1.9 mm (L) / 3.5 mm (R). This is skin deformation; the IK targets are fixed.
- **Kick top clearance 35.9 → 42.1 cm** (the foot still rising). **Knee-raise hold 22.1 → 25.1 cm.** Both ≥ 10 cm, asserted.
- The lifting foot clears the floor by ≥ 0.2 mm at lift-off and landing.

**Interpenetration** (exact edge-through-triangle test on the shipped mesh, all frames, both directions): **0 intersecting frames** for forearm/hand × {torso, both thighs} and shin × {other shin, other thigh}.
- Closest approaches: hand–torso 0.8 cm, hand–thigh 4.9 cm, shin–shin 8.3 cm.

**Other checks:**
- **Quaternions:** w ≥ 0; minimum consecutive dot 0.9973, across the wrap 0.9999; int16 error ≤ 0.003°.
- **Round-trip:** `read_pack2` returns header, faces and skin exactly; rest vertices within half a step; skinning again matches to 0.0007 mm.
- **three.js:** `applyBoneTransform` matches the Python LBS to ≤ 0.0008 mm (frames 0, 198, 465, 594, 726).

## Record: v2a (`taiji-sequence-v2a.bin`, 504 frames, 16.8 s)
- **Timing:** 12-frame smoothstep cross-fades and the generated clips at their original speed.
- **Error:** LBS vs exact max 17.1 / p99 9.3 mm.
- **Speed:** max joint speed 14.9 °/frame.
- **Kick and raise:** kick 1.47 s with a 7-frame top; knee-raise hold 2.0 s, fully static except the arms.
- **Bows:** front 36–39°, rear 16–22°, sink 6.0–6.4 cm.
- **Checks:** all contact and intersection checks passed.

## Doubts
1. **Still no stepping.** The feet stay on two fixed spots, so 野马分鬃 / 搂膝拗步 / 倒卷肱 bow in place inside a wide stance rather than stepping into each bow.
2. **The opening form is quiet below the waist.** 天地合一 has symmetric arms, so the waist barely turns there (yaw ≈ −2° for 3 s). The body still sinks, sways and breathes. The kick's standing leg is also nearly fixed for 1.5 s (support knee 20°).
3. **Generated arms in 野马分鬃 / 搂膝拗步 still hang low.** The right-shoulder clearance bump (≤ 24°) can read as an elbow-out arm.
4. **Kick extension is the fastest motion** (8.5 °/frame at the knee).
5. **Plain LBS creases** the groin at 70–80° hip flexion and the raised-arm shoulder (≤ 1.7 cm vs exact). Not visible at hero scale.
6. **Smoothing lowers some peaks slightly.** Example: the left-shoulder peak at ~7 s, 72 → 66°, partly the clearance bump.
7. **The hold sway is ±1.2 cm after smoothing** (±1.5 cm designed).

## Reproduce
```
PY=~/Documents/GitHub/smplx_meridian_project/.venv/bin/python
$PY tools/motion_pack.py contact --out <scratch>/v2/contact
$PY tools/motion_pack.py build2 --out <dir> --bin-name taiji-sequence-arms-only.bin                          # arms-only
$PY tools/motion_pack.py build2 --arm-scale 1.3 --choreo --planted-tol-mm 2 --out <dir>                       # v2a (rename to -v2a)
$PY tools/motion_pack.py build2 --v2b --arm-scale 1.3 --lead 9 --follow-ref 0.12 --planted-tol-mm 2 \
    --out shared/assets/motion --stats <scratch>/v2d/final_stats.json --dump <scratch>/v2d/final_dump.npz \
    --plot shared/assets/motion/curves-v2b.png                                                                 # shipped v2b
~/tools/.venv/bin/python tools/motion_pack.py preview2 --bin shared/assets/motion/taiji-sequence.bin \
    --workdir <scratch>/v2d/www --png-dir shared/assets/motion --n 12 --compare-dump <scratch>/v2d/final_dump.npz
```

# v3 — `taiji-umons-f.bin` / `taiji-umons-m.bin` (recorded motion, two bodies, `hmmh-motion-2`)

Research record with all experiments, figures and the problems found: `research/2026-10-02-taiji-real-motion/README.md`.

## What ships
- **`taiji-umons-f.bin`** (369,532 B): SMPL-X **female** body, played in the hero. 1,751 frames = 58.4 s at 30 fps.
- **`taiji-umons-m.bin`** (312,504 B): SMPL-X **male** body, played in Home 01 / card A. 1,349 frames = 45.0 s at 30 fps.
  Its header also carries `bands` for the card B functional panel (about 16 KB of the 20 KB header).
- **The motion is derived from recordings of people, not procedurally generated.** Source: UMONS-TAICHI (Tits, Laraba,
  Caulier, Tilmanne, Dutoit 2018, *Data in Brief* 19, doi:10.1016/j.dib.2018.05.088; Zenodo record 2784581; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
  Single trials were read out of `Segmented_TSV.zip` (the Qualisys optical capture: 68 markers, 179 Hz) by HTTP range
  requests (about 306 MB fetched in total, against 3.6 GB for the whole zip).
- **One performer per body**, chosen by the medoid rule restricted to that sex (sexes from the dataset's `Metadata.txt`):
  - female P03 (Expert, skill 8.67);
  - male P06 (Advanced, skill 8.5).
- **Same layout and fields as v2**, so the viewer needs no format change. The header adds a few fields (see `shared/MOTION_FORMAT.md`, v3 note):
  - `citation`;
  - `groundYNote`, because `groundY` is now the planted-foot level;
  - `segments[].trial`;
  - `bands` (male pack only).
- Previews:
  - `preview-umons-f-00 … 07.png` and `preview-umons-m-00 … 07.png`, 8 evenly spaced times;
  - `curves-umons.png`: wrist height, knee flexion and pelvis yaw, v2b against v3.
- Kept unchanged: `taiji-sequence.bin` (v2b) and every earlier pack. **v2b still rebuilds byte-identically** with the edited `tools/motion_pack.py` (checked 2026-10-02).

## Provenance
| part | source |
|---|---|
| joint rotations of every recorded segment | **recorded**. Joint centres come from the markers: hip = Harrington 2007 from ASIS/PSIS; knee, ankle, elbow and wrist = epicondyle / malleolus / styloid midpoints; glenohumeral centre = acromion plus a fitted offset. Segment axes come from the epicondyle, styloid, metacarpal and foot markers; pelvis, thorax and head frames from their markers. A torch fit of the 22 SMPL-X rotations matches bone directions and axes. |
| standing calibration | each participant's G01 (Wuji) trials map quiet standing to the SMPL-X rest pose (pelvis, thorax, head, trunk, feet; sagittal only) |
| gaze | a constant neck/head pitch per trial so the median head elevation is −2°. P03 needed −3 … +2°; P06 +9.5 … +20.7°, because his headband sat differently than in the calibration take. |
| root path | the data pelvis path scaled to the model leg length, then a least-squares solve that keeps contact points still |
| feet | contacts from the heel and metatarsal markers (heel within 1.5 cm of the trial floor level, forefoot within 3 cm, < 0.15 m/s). A torch polish keeps flagged contact points still and on the floor and every sole point above it. Corrections are low-frequency, and contact weights fade in and out over about 2 frames. |
| transitions between forms | **synthesised**: 0, 1 or 2 planned steps, 1.8 s per step: weight onto the support foot first, a low swing (≤ 3.5 cm), heel-first landing, then the weight follows. The upper body blends with matched end velocities. The steps are chosen so the body faces the camera side and stays centred. The loop closes exactly. |
| hand / leg clearance | automatic, because the SMPL-X template is not the performer's shape. The shoulder turns the arm away from the body (female left ≤ 12° over 77 frames, male right ≤ 24° over 127 frames). The free leg is abducted at the hip (male ≤ 18°), and with both feet down the knees swivel (male ≤ 6°). |
| loop start | frame 0 = the opening form's flat-footed frame with the lowest hands (female: recorded frame 141 of G04; male: 135) |

The p90 / max slides come from long contact runs of 10–25 s, which include the pivots on heel or ball that the forms contain;
a fixed sole vertex then moves by the pivot radius. The worst runs are noted in the research README.

**LBS vs exact, per segment** (max / p99 mm):

| form | female | male |
|---|---|---|
| G04 | 20.7 / 7.5 | 17.0 / 8.1 |
| G08 | 17.1 / 8.7 | 21.1 / 9.2 |
| G12 | 17.6 / 8.3 | 21.1 / 11.0 |
| G06 | 20.9 / 9.1 | 22.6 / 10.4 |
| G07 | 18.8 / 9.0 | 17.5 / 9.7 |
| G09 + seam | 18.3 / 10.5 | 20.4 / 11.7 |
| G04 (tail) | 22.0 / 10.1 | 18.1 / 9.9 |

The worst parts are the elbows and hips (no pose correctives in LBS).

**Interpolation (L3).** The viewer slerps between pack frames. Cubic Catmull-Rom on the quaternions at 120 Hz display times
differs from it by at most **0.98 mm** (female) and **0.99 mm** (male); p99 is 0.52 / 0.37 mm. That is under the 1 mm rule,
so **slerp stays**. For reference, a 15 fps copy of the pack would be off by 3.5 / 3.4 mm max.

normalise after decode","rootTranslationNote":"int16 millimetres; pelvis path from the recording (scaled to the model's leg length), solved so contact feet stay still on groundY","motionNote":"derived from recordings of a person (UMONS-TAICHI Qualisys optical motion capture (68 markers, 179 Hz); medoid trials of skilled performers), fitted to a parametric body (SMPL-X joint rotations from bone directions and segment axes), light smoothing, feet cleaned with a contact detector and leg IK; not procedurally generated","citation":"Tits M, Laraba S, Caulier E, Tilmanne J, Dutoit T (2018). UMONS-TAICHI: a multimodal motion capture dataset of expertise in Taijiquan gestures. Data in Brief 19, 1214-1221. doi:10.1016/j.dib.2018.05.088; Zenodo record 2784581; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0","bands":{"step":3,"units":{"wristHeight":"m","kneeFlexion":"deg","pelvisYaw":"deg"},"performers":{"G04":12,"G08":12,"G12":12,"G06":12,"G07":12,"G09":12},"note":"across-performer mean and SD (one UMONS-TAICHI Qualisys trial per participant and form, D01, time-normalised and aligned to each recorded segment; null in the transitions). wristHeight = mean of both wrist centres above the floor, scaled by model stature / performer stature; kneeFlexion = mean of both knees, 180 - hip-knee-ankle angle; pelvisYaw = hip-line facing relative to the trial's mean facing. Compute the same from the pack's joints (wrists 20/21 above groundY; hips 1/2, knees 4/5, ankles 7/8).","series":"<elided: wristHeight / kneeFlexion / pelvisYaw, each {mean:[450], sd:[450]}, null in transitions>"}}
```

## Reproduce
Each `motion` run fits root and feet with the torch polish (defaults: `--w-dsmooth 3e4 --soft-sigma 2`) and levels the gaze to −2°.
```
PY=~/Documents/GitHub/smplx_meridian_project/.venv/bin/python     # torch and open3d: never import torch first in one process
T=tools/umons_motion.py; MP=tools/motion_pack.py; S=<scratch>/motion-v3
# data: Zenodo 2784581 Segmented_Kinect.zip (screening only); single Segmented_TSV.zip members via scratch/work/fetch_tsv.py (range reads)

# 1. per trial: fit, then root + feet
$PY $T fit    --trial P03T02C14G08D01S01 --source qualisys --gender FEMALE --tsv-dir $S/raw/tsv --out $S/seq/fits/P03T02C14G08D01S01_q_F.npz
$PY $T motion --fit $S/seq/fits/P03T02C14G08D01S01_q_F.npz --out $S/seq/fits/P03T02C14G08D01S01_q_F_motion.npz

# 2. loop: --motions = the six motion npz in play order (G04, G08, G12, G06, G07, G09)
$PY $T sequence --motions <G04,G08,G12,G06,G07,G09 motion npz> --out $S/seq/seq_F_q.npz

# 3. clearance, then polish, then (male only) the card B bands, then the pack
$PY $MP build3 --clear 16 --clear-out $S/seq/seq_F_c.npz --motion $S/seq/seq_F_q.npz --out $S/pack --bin-name tmp.bin
$PY $T polish --seq $S/seq/seq_F_c.npz --out $S/seq/seq_F_cp.npz
$PY $T bands  --seq $S/seq/seq_M_cp.npz --out $S/seq/seq_M_cpb.npz --list $S/work/band_trials.txt --tsv-dir $S/raw/tsv
$PY $MP build3 --clear 6 --motion $S/seq/seq_F_cp.npz --out shared/assets/motion --bin-name taiji-umons-f.bin --stats <stats.json> --dump <dump.npz>
```
The scripts `<scratch>/motion-v3/seq/finalize.sh` and `make_seqs.sh` hold the exact runs. The research README lists every trial id.
